topic: Your RTX 3090 is still an AI workhorse
title: RTX 3090 Still Runs Local AI: The One Spec That Decides What Fits
description: Your RTX 3090 is still an AI workhorse for local AI, and a basement project proves it. A builder turned thirteen and a half million Reddit and Hacker News opinions into a site called Trust Me Bro Reviews, ranked products with the shills filtered out, using pairs of NVLinked RTX 3090s running a Gemma mixture-of-experts model with vLLM. Everyone assumed 2020 cards were obsolete, but the spec that decides what runs is VRAM capacity, and the 3090's 24 GB of GDDR6X matches an RTX 4090 exactly. You'll learn why memory capacity decides which models fit on your card, where the honest wall sits as giant models crawl at about five tokens a second, and why the catches (FP8 hardware, power draw, and the pairs qualifier) don't change the verdict. If a 3090 sits in your tower, watch this before you upgrade. Subscribe to Build Local AI for more. (Narration is AI-generated.)
hook_candidates: A basement. Pairs of 3090s. One ranked half the internet.
Your 3090 matches a 4090 at the one spec that decides what runs.
2020 called. Its GPU still runs 2026 models.
Thirteen million Reddit opinions, ranked by a six-year-old card.
The cheapest 24 GB card is still the one you own.
Everyone called it obsolete. Then it shipped a product.
One spec decides what your PC can run. Yours is fine.
RTX 3090: too old for AI, or exactly enough?
Seventy-billion models say no. Twenty-four gigabytes says yes.
narration_full: A guy in a basement ranked half the internet's product advice. The cards are pairs of thirty nineties from twenty twenty. The same card sits in your tower. His site is called Trust Me Bro Reviews. It reads Reddit and Hacker News opinions, filters out the shills and fake praise, and ranks what people actually love. Thirteen and a half million opinions became a ranked list of products, places and tools. His cards are RTX thirty nineties, a generation the internet loves to bury. Every AI video lately has called that card obsolete, too old and too slow for local models. The comments said buy a newer card or go home. Here is what actually ran in that basement. Pairs of thirty nineties, joined by NVLink, a direct cable that links one card straight to another. vLLM, an open-source serving engine, fed a Gemma mixture-of-experts model, many specialists with a few awake per word. What decides what runs on your card is VRAM, the memory on the card itself. If a model fits inside it, the model runs. Your thirty ninety carries twenty-four gigabytes of memory. The newer card carries the same. The honest wall is real. A seventy-billion-parameter LLaMA squeezes into that memory, then crawls slower than reading speed. Tokens are word-pieces, the chunks a model speaks in. His giant job also ran on pairs, never one card. The newer card is faster, with built-in hardware for a compact number format yours will never get. Picture an old pickup: same bed as the new truck, same loads, more fuel, no turbo. It breaks when the load outgrows the bed. One spec decides what fits, and on that spec your card still matches. Obsolete meant not enough memory, and yours never had that problem. It's old, not obsolete.

analogy.vehicle: an old heavy-duty pickup next to this year's sports-trim truck
analogy.mapping: the pickup bed is the card's memory capacity, identical in size to the new truck's bed, so it hauls the same loads; the extra fuel is the higher power draw; the missing turbo is the newer FP8 hardware
analogy.limit: the analogy breaks when the load grows past the bed, meaning models that need more memory than any 3090 or 4090 carries, or when the job is paid by the hour at scale and the speed gap compounds

notes_for_review: 'Thirteen and a half million opinions' rounds the exact 13,576,547, and 'about five tokens a second' rounds 5.2 tok/s; both exact digits appear on screen only in their own scenes. The pairs qualifier holds wherever the basement job is cited: scene four reveals the NVLinked pairs, scene six repeats it, and the single-card lesson is framed purely as memory capacity, never as one card doing his job. The pickup analogy's limit is spoken inside scene seven itself: it breaks when the load outgrows the bed. No other brief quantities (product count, wattage, bandwidth, the speed-gap percentage) are spoken or shown anywhere.
